tools.name: book_consult
tools.description: Books one of yesmcp's consultation windows for the user. Requires the `slotId` from list_availability plus the user's name, email address and the topic they want to discuss. Before calling this tool, tell the user in plain words what booking stores and why: yesmcp stores their name, their email addr

tools.name: cancel_booking
tools.description: Cancels one of yesmcp's consultation bookings and frees the window for others. Requires the booking reference from the confirmation email AND the email address the booking was made with — ask the user for both before calling. Confirm with the user that they really want to cancel before you call this

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "book_consult" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: book_consult, advise_scenarios, demo_walkthrough, directory_census, booking_widget, services_widget · Private data: list_availability, get_services, demo_walkthrough · Public sink: book_consult, cancel_booking, reschedule_booking, booking_widget · Destructive: advise_scenarios.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: book_consult, advise_scenarios, demo_walkthrough, directory_census, booking_widget, services_widget · Private data: list_availability, get_services, demo_walkthrough · Public sink: book_consult, cancel_booking, reschedule_booking, booking_widget · Destructive: advise_scenarios

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
